title: Docker Sandbox Kit Spec: Packaging AI Agent Permissions as OCI Images
gist: Docker is donating its v3 Sandbox Kit spec to the CNCF, packaging AI agent permissions (hosts, credentials, volumes) as ordinary OCI images so they can be reviewed, signed and pinned. Enforcement relies on the runtime, and Docker Sandboxes is the only conforming one so far.

themes.theme: Docker donates Sandbox Kit spec to CNCF

insights.claim: Docker announced it is bringing the Sandbox Kit Specification (Apache 2.0, now at v3) to the CNCF, aiming to make what an AI agent may access as portable as the agent itself; the announcement came at WeAreDevelopers on September 24.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Watch whether the CNCF accepts the spec and at what maturity level; it signals standards-setting for agent security.
insights.locator: Docker has announced that it is bringing

insights.claim: Docker draws a parallel to its earlier donation of the image format and runc that led to OCI, positioning Kits as the next standardization play for the container ecosystem.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Docker is repeating a playbook of donating formats to own the ecosystem default around agent runtimes.

insights.claim: Docker says it built Kits with AWS, Box, Datadog, Dynatrace, JFrog, NanoClaw, OpenClaw, Palo Alto Networks, and Snyk, among others, and CNCF CTO Chris Aniszczyk publicly welcomed the move.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: A broad security and observability vendor list suggests ecosystem buy-in, though only Docker implements a runtime so far.
insights.locator: Docker says it built Kits with AWS

insights.claim: The posts do not say whether the spec has been accepted into a CNCF program or which maturity level it would enter, so the CNCF 'donation' is not yet a formal acceptance.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Treat the CNCF framing cautiously until a formal program acceptance is announced.
insights.quote: The posts do not say whether the spec has been accepted into a CNCF program or which maturity level it would enter.

themes.theme: Agent permissions as a reviewable artifact

insights.claim: Agents such as Claude Code and Codex install packages, call APIs, and use credentials on a user's behalf, yet their grants (bind mounts, broad tokens, opened firewall rules) usually live in shell history, dashboards, and memory rather than a reviewable artifact.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Unreviewable agent permissions are a governance gap that creates demand for agent security and policy tooling.
insights.locator: Agents such as Claude Code and Codex

insights.claim: Docker argues that fragmentation of agent permission handling is what OCI was created to prevent, and that every runtime vendor could otherwise invent its own answer.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Without a standard, expect vendor lock-in competition around agent sandbox formats.
insights.locator: Docker argues this is the fragmentation

insights.claim: Pinning a Kit's digest pins content and permissions together, so the permission set of an agent becomes immutable and auditable like any container image.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Enables supply-chain style controls (pin, sign, diff) on agent permissions.
insights.quote: Pinning the digest pins content and permissions together.

insights.claim: In v3 a Kit is an ordinary OCI image with no custom media type and no sidecar file, declared by a single manifest entry (vnd.docker.sandbox.kit.descriptor), so it can be built with docker buildx build, pulled with docker pull, scanned, signed, or used in a FROM.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Existing registries, scanners and signing tools work unchanged, lowering adoption cost and favoring incumbents like JFrog and Snyk.
insights.locator: In v3, a Kit is no longer

insights.claim: Declarations are typed, versioned capabilities such as com.docker.sandbox/network-policy@2 and com.docker.sandbox/credential@1; in the GitHub CLI example the Kit allows api.github.com but denies DELETE on /repos/**, since deny wins.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Fine-grained, deny-wins network policy per agent is a template for least-privilege agent design.

insights.claim: Credentials can be proxy-managed: a conforming runtime injects the real token into requests to named domains while only a sentinel value exists inside the sandbox, keeping secrets out of the agent's reach.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Mitigates credential exfiltration by compromised or prompt-injected agents.
insights.quote: only a sentinel value exists inside the sandbox

insights.claim: A launch combines one workload Kit supplying the root filesystem with any number of mixin overlays, ordered by a provides/requires dependency graph; resolution fails if a requires is unmet or two Kits provide the same name, network rules are unioned, and incompatible declarations are errors.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Composable permission overlays mimic package-manager dependency semantics.
insights.locator: A launch combines one workload Kit

insights.claim: Every descriptor reduces to a normalized set of grants, so a runtime that gates updates can record that set and block any version that widens it, including one that removes a deny rule.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Enables permission-diff gating for agent updates, a security-review primitive.

insights.claim: A Kit only requests permissions and the host decides; without a conforming runtime the annotation is inert, and a launch is refused if a required request cannot be satisfied.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Security value depends on runtime enforcement, not the spec itself.

insights.claim: Docker Sandboxes, which run agents in microVMs with their own kernel, is currently the only conforming runtime, so portability across runtimes has not been demonstrated.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Open-standard claims are unproven until a second runtime implements the spec; a key adoption milestone to watch.
insights.quote: portability across different runtimes has not yet been demonstrated
insights.locator: It is important to note that enforcement

insights.claim: Docker will keep maintaining the specification until governance changes, and two conformance suites (one for Kit artifacts, one for runtimes) ship with it; the descriptor grammar and per-capability semantics are new and require learning.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Docker retains control for now; conformance suites are the path for third-party runtimes.
